Daniel — thanks, this is clear. Looping in Kim (privacy/controls lead) and Marissa (ops/implementation) to provide the artifacts and the diagram. High-level answers inline below; we'll follow up with the workbook and a short diagram.

1) KMS model: Hosted API uses Redwood-managed keys by default (we store model state and logs encrypted with a Redwood Service Key). For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed CMEK (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) — we can provide a diagram and the KMCS usage matrix.

2) Routing/failover: For US customers in the hosted product, normal traffic stays in US regions. Failover routing can go to an alternate region (e.g., us-west -> us-east). We do not route US customer traffic to EU data centers unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region failover to an EU region. We'll attach the routing policy excerpt and SLOs.

3) Logs/retention: We retain request/response metadata and token-level cost attribution for 90 days by default; extended retention enterprise add-on available. We will add the log schema sample.

Kim/Marissa — can you take the workbook items and return completed tabs for items marked 'evidence' + a KMS diagram (PNG) by EOD Tue 11/04? Thanks.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Thu, Oct 30, 2025 at 12:03 PM, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Daniel — thanks, this is clear. Looping in Kim (privacy/controls lead) and Marissa (ops/implementation) to provide the artifacts and the diagram.

Hi Daniel — attaching the completed evidence tabs and the KMS diagram. Notes: 

- KMS usage matrix: Hosted (service-managed keys) = default. Dedicated/Private = customer-managed keys (CMEK) supported for data-at-rest and for envelope encryption of stored cache/shards. Customer CMKs can be enforced via an enterprise onboarding checklist and IAM role binding.
- On-prem package: in fully air-gapped installs the customer is the root key holder; Redwood provides key-rotation guidance and an offline key-initialization script.
- Failover routing: Redwood's Smart Routing policy routes within the same legal region by default and only crosses regions on configured cross-region failover policies (explicit opt-in). We will supply the excerpt from the routing policy and the specific failover SLO numbers (p95 failover < 120s for critical control plane operations).
- Audit logs: example schema included (timestamp, request_id, model_id, customer_id, route, action, user_agent, ip, token_count, cost_center). Default retention: 90 days; enterprise retention tiers: 1 year / 3 years / custom on request.

Attachments included: completed-edge-dpf-template.xlsx, kms-diagram.png

Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Daniel — following up with a couple of implementation clarifications that Procurement asked us to confirm: 

- Encryption in transit: TLS1.2+ with mTLS available for Dedicated and Private deployments. We will provide an mTLS config snippet for SRE integration.
- Subprocessor routing: We do use cloud provider-managed networking for hosted; subprocessor list in the workbook is current.
- Operational readiness: onboarding runbook (Ops) and a sample SOC 2 extract are included in the workbook. For Dedicated customers we provide a post-commit runbook for KMS rotation and key rollover windows (recommended: quarterly rotation, 72h roll window).
